frequency_question: How often do formal agency recognition revocation proceedings initiated by a federal department result in final revocation within a short operational window?
membership_rule: Includes any instance where a federal department or supervisory agency formally evaluated, initiated review of, or moved to strip a recognized accrediting or delegated authority, excluding routine renewals without adverse findings.

cases.name: American Bar Association accreditation review challenges by Department of Education advisory committees
ACICS (Accrediting Council for Independent Colleges and Schools) initial withdrawal of recognition
ACICS final termination of federal recognition after administrative appeals

coverage_note: 3 named major contested agency recognition proceedings; universe of highly contested federal accrediting revocations is small.
known_gaps: Does not fully capture informal settlements or back-room compliance resolutions that do not reach the formal final order stage.
skeleton: Recognized accrediting agency review cycles over past three decades involving major compliance disputes, multiplied by the historical proportion resulting in actual terminal revocation within a sub-year timeframe.
multiplier: 3 major contested federal accrediting agency challenge cycles evaluated, out of which terminal revocations occurred in 2 instances over the long term, yielding a baseline historical transition rate of roughly 1 in 3 for severe challenge proceedings.
validity_reason: Regulatory standards and administrative procedures for agency recognition review remain stable across multi-year departmental cycles.
